content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Database migration workflows must plan ordering, compatibility, backups, failure recovery, and whether schema changes should be separated from application rollout. Deployment workflows should promote a known artifact through controlled environments, restrict credentials and concurrency, verify health, and define rollback conditions before production use. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Separating schema changes from application release steps when needed
items.text: Match the event to the intended lifecycle, then test positive and negative branch/path/activity cases. Event payloads may be attacker-controlled, and scheduled jobs use UTC rather than a guaranteed exact start time.

content_blocks.code:
jobs:
  deploy-staging:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - run: echo "Verify known artifact before deploy"
content_blocks.expected_output: The job is associated with the staging environment and read-only repository access; actual deployment credentials and environment protections must be configured separately.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain database deployment workflows, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Move known build outputs through controlled environments with auditable approvals and recovery plans.

content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Database migration workflows must plan ordering, compatibility, backups, failure recovery, and whether schema changes should be separated from application rollout. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.
